Let
\[
a=\frac{1-\gamma}{1+\gamma},\qquad b=\frac{1-4\gamma}{1+4\gamma}.
\]
Then
\[
R_A=\begin{pmatrix}a&0\\0&b\end{pmatrix}.
\]
The matrix \(B\) has eigenvalues \(2,9\), with eigenvectors \((1,1)\) and \((1,-1)\). Hence if
\[
c=\frac{1-2\gamma}{1+2\gamma},\qquad d=\frac{1-9\gamma}{1+9\gamma},
\]
then \(R_B\) has trace \(c+d\) and determinant \(cd\). For
\[
M=R_BR_A,
\]
we get
\[
\operatorname{tr}M=\frac{(a+b)(c+d)}2,\qquad \det M=abcd.
\]
Writing
\[
P=(1+\gamma)(1+2\gamma)(1+4\gamma)(1+9\gamma),
\]
one computes
\[
\operatorname{tr}M=
\frac{2(1-4\gamma^2)(1-18\gamma^2)}{P},
\]
and
\[
\det M=
\frac{(1-\gamma)(1-2\gamma)(1-4\gamma)(1-9\gamma)}{P}.
\]

The eigenvalues of \(T_\gamma=\frac12(I+M)\) are \(\frac12(1+\mu_1),\frac12(1+\mu_2)\), where \(\mu_i\) are the eigenvalues of \(M\). The discriminant of the characteristic polynomial of \(M\) is
\[
(\operatorname{tr}M)^2-4\det M
=
\frac{4\gamma^2(3700\gamma^4-1157\gamma^2+58)}{P^2}.
\]
Since
\[
3700u^2-1157u+58
=3700\left(u-\frac{58}{925}\right)\left(u-\frac14\right),
\]
the eigenvalues are complex conjugates precisely when
\[
\frac{58}{925}<\gamma^2<\frac14.
\]
In that interval,
\[
r(T_\gamma)^2=\det T_\gamma
=\frac{1+\operatorname{tr}M+\det M}{4}.
\]
A simplification gives
\[
\det T_\gamma
=
\frac{4+110\gamma^2+288\gamma^4}{4P}.
\]
Let
\[
h(\gamma)=\det T_\gamma.
\]
Then
\[
h'(\gamma)=\frac{F(\gamma)}{P^2},
\]
where
\[
F(x)=9648x^6+7128x^5-229x^4+38x^2-99x-16.
\]

We now locate the unique critical point relevant to the minimum. For \(0<x\le 1/3\),
\[
F(x)<0.
\]
Also
\[
F'(x)=57888x^5+35640x^4-916x^3+76x-99>0
\]
for \(x\ge 1/3\). Since
\[
F(1/3)<0,\qquad F(3/8)>0,
\]
there is exactly one zero of \(F\) in \((1/3,3/8)\), and \(h\) decreases before it and increases after it.

Outside the complex-eigenvalue interval, \(r(T_\gamma)\ge \sqrt{\det T_\gamma}\), so the same critical point gives the global minimum of \(r(T_\gamma)\).

Therefore the unique minimizing value is
\[
\boxed{
\operatorname{root}\!\left(
9648x^6+7128x^5-229x^4+38x^2-99x-16;\,
\frac13,\frac38
\right)
}.
\]
Numerically, this is approximately
\[
\gamma\approx 0.3416258707.
\]
